note: Published US income-mobility benchmarks for the decade's ladder (percent of a starting fifth). The model's own panel is synthetic and ranks households of every age; the closest analogue is the Treasury's closed panel of taxpayers 25+ with fifths ranked within the panel. From Tools/history/sources.json (research collected 2026-10-22, each number read in its cited source).

decade.label: US Treasury, taxpayers 25+, 1996-2005, fifths ranked within the panel
decade.source: U.S. Department of the Treasury (Nov 13, 2007; revised March 2008), "Income Mobility in the U.S. from 1996 to 2005," https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/131/Report-Income-Mobility-2008.pdf (Table 2, p.9).

decade.label: US Treasury, taxpayers 25+, 1996-2005, fifths of all taxpayers
decade.years: 1996 -> 2005 (9-year span, often described as a decade)
decade.source: U.S. Department of the Treasury (Nov 13, 2007; revised March 2008), "Income Mobility in the U.S. from 1996 to 2005," https://home.treasury.gov/system/files/131/Report-Income-Mobility-2008.pdf (Table 1, p.7).

decade.label: Auten & Gee, tax returns 25+, 1996-2005, size-adjusted
decade.source: Auten & Gee (2009), "Income Mobility in the United States: New Evidence from Income Tax Data," National Tax Journal 62(2): 301-328 (Table 2 p.307; Table 6 p.313; Table 5 p.312). DOI 10.17310/ntj.2009.2.05.

decade.label: PSID, after-tax family income, 1990-1999
decade.source: Hungerford, CRS Report RL34434 (2008), Table 2 panel B, p.CRS-10 (same URL as psidHungerford1980s).

decade.label: PSID, after-tax family income, 1980-1989
decade.source: Hungerford, CRS Report RL34434, "Income Inequality, Income Mobility, and Economic Policy: U.S. Trends in the 1980s and 1990s" (Apr 4, 2008), Table 2 panel A, p.CRS-10, https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/20080404_RL34434_be64d1aab381920155131bf341304806355ba3b7.pdf

decade.label: PSID family heads and spouses, 1995-2005 (Bradbury 2011)
decade.source: Bradbury (2011), "Trends in U.S. Family Income Mobility, 1969-2006," Federal Reserve Bank of Boston Working Paper 11-10, Table 2 p.38, https://www.bostonfed.org/-/media/Documents/Workingpapers/PDF/economic/wp/wp2011/wp1110.pdf

generations.label: Chetty, Hendren, Kline & Saez 2014: children born 1980-82 at ~30 against their parents
generations.source: Chetty, Hendren, Kline & Saez (2014), "Where is the Land of Opportunity? The Geography of Intergenerational Mobility in the United States," Quarterly Journal of Economics 129(4): 1553-1623. Read: NBER WP 19843 https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w19843/w19843.pdf and authors' QJE version https://opportunityinsights.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/mobility_geo.pdf (Table II).

jobLoss.label: displaced workers lose about 25% of earnings the first year in an expansion, 39% in a recession (Davis & von Wachter 2011)
jobLoss.source: Davis & von Wachter (2011), "Recessions and the Costs of Job Loss," Brookings Papers on Economic Activity, Fall 2011: 1-72 (abstract; Table 1 p.22; text p.17), https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2011/09/2011b_bpea_davis.pdf

divorce.label: household income falls 41% for women and 23% for men after a late-life divorce (GAO 2012)
divorce.source: U.S. GAO (July 2012), GAO-12-699, "Retirement Security: Women Still Face Challenges," p.28 and Table 19 p.84, https://www.gao.gov/assets/gao-12-699.pdf

health.label: earnings fall about 20% over three years after a hospital admission (Dobkin et al. 2018)
health.source: Dobkin, Finkelstein, Kluender & Notowidigdo (2018), "The Economic Consequences of Hospital Admissions," American Economic Review 108(2): 308-352 (Table 2 p.323; pp.311, 333, 336), https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/114039

poverty.label: 37% of poverty spells begin when the head's earnings fall; about 11% with a move to a female-headed family (Bane & Ellwood)
poverty.source: Bane & Ellwood (1983), NBER Working Paper 1199, Table 3 p.21, https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w1199/w1199.pdf ; published as "Slipping into and out of Poverty: The Dynamics of Spells," Journal of Human Resources 21(1): 1-23 (1986).
